name: Karbonsteel Engineering Limited
sector: Heavy and precision structural steel fabrication
summary:
Karbonsteel is a heavy and precision structural-steel fabricator with genuine industrial demand, a substantial order pipeline and a meaningful capacity expansion. Revenue reached ₹300.88 crore in FY26 and the comparable FY23–FY26 CAGR is 24.59%. The investment thesis is a cyclical industrial expansion and execution-recovery situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. At the secondary 19 October 2026 close of ₹104.10, headline earnings and enterprise multiples appear moderate, but reliability and current funding cannot be assumed from those multiples. [S01][S02][Q1]

Classification: Hold — unresolved. Historical factor points support BQS 5.00 and GQS 6.30; IAS is NS and the G2/G3 holds exclude investment ranking. The decisive concern is the combination of inconsistent cash-flow disclosures, incomplete audit-annexure reporting and current credit-information gaps. The annual report's ₹3.6004 crore cash reconciliation discrepancy is exactly explained numerically by a different capex figure in the earlier results; it is not evidence of cash theft. That counterevidence materially reduces the severity of the interpretation, but does not by itself correct the latest annual report. The FY25 CFO variants now have a full numerical bridge; creditor and maturity regroupings explain most balance-sheet presentation changes without validating every underlying opening classification. [S01][S10]

A credible improvement requires a corrected/reconciled statutory package, demonstrably usable liquidity after capex and maturities, commissioning evidence and sustainable per-share profit/cash outcomes. A lower price alone cannot clear those requirements. The strongest positive countercase is that the cash inconsistency is a reporting error, debt has already fallen after the IPO, the expansion is commissioned successfully and the concentrated customer book pays on time. Those outcomes should be tested, not assumed. All ordinary return/entry-price outputs remain null. The tested conditional funding cases also breach under their disclosed operating assumptions, not because a cash reserve is known to be legally required. A separately labeled recapitalization model is only an analytical illustration.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The exact issuer is Karbonsteel Engineering Limited, BSE SME security 544511, security ID KARBON, ISIN INE0V8A01016, formerly Karbon Steelmart Private Limited and subsequently Karbonsteel Engineering Private Limited. The issuer listed on 16 September 2025. The official 19 October interoperability master contains KARBON$ in SM with an 800-share lot and 14,141,822 issued shares; this does not make the company NSE-listed. The analysis cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata. The price reference is the 19 October secondary historical close ₹104.10, not a live offer. Market capitalization is ₹147.2164 crore. [S01][S02][M1][Q1]

Scope is standalone because no consolidated operating subsidiary perimeter is established in these statements. The results explicitly use Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not mandatory Ind AS; a cash-flow footnote mentioning Ind AS 7 is inconsistent boilerplate and does not change the accounting basis. Units are ₹crore, unless otherwise labeled. The investor horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 with actual calendar-day weights, nominal 15% pretax equity hurdle and an illustrative ₹5 lakh position, not a portfolio recommendation. [S10][S11]

G1 is Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold and G4 Conditional. There is no evidenced governance failure or reported bank default. Identity and retrieved document values are high-confidence; interpretation of current financial reliability and available funding is Low. Aggregate incremental-capital evidence is Medium confidence, with maturity and cash-classification sensitivities. Growth, business positioning and dated operating history are Medium. Liquidity is incomplete and overall investment confidence is Low. The presence of a full audit report and a clean main opinion is not a shortcut around reading CARO, IFC and cash reconciliations.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 5. R, D, P and L are NS. CAP is supported by a same-perimeter multi-year investment bridge, not a current ROCE shortcut. CASH is grounded in both reported and financing-adjusted conversion. These separate judgments do not pretend the full statutory package is reliable enough for an investment conclusion. GQS means Growth Quality; P is price-implied expectations, not predictability. [S01][S02][S10]

Exact Decimal arithmetic gives BQS 5.00 and GQS 6.30, both with full factor coverage. IAS reuses the unrounded BQS exactly: Q contributes 1.2500 with 25% coverage; missing R/D/P/L yield mathematical bounds 2.0000–8.7500. IAS remains NS, not the midpoint or a renormalized score. Every weight and contribution is embedded. G2/G3 holds exclude the issuer from investment rankings even though historical quality points can now be calculated. [S01][S04][M1][Q1]

No governance cap applies because GOV exceeds 3 and G1 does not fail. No funding-failure cap applies because a verified actual funding failure has not been established. CAP 5 and CASH 4 do not trigger the framework's ≤3 growth-quality cap. The revised points follow new reconciliation work, not an attempt to raise a score: CAP's mixed 11.0–11.6% whole-window proxy and prior stronger returns are evidenced; weak cash remaining after financing is also evidenced. These are framework judgments with Medium confidence, not validated predictors.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company designs, fabricates and assembles customized heavy and precision steel structures for industrial plants, refineries, steel mills, railway bridges, oil and gas, chemicals and other infrastructure. Revenue comes from fabricated structures and fabrication services, with a history of steel trading during pandemic disruption. FY26 accounting is a single business segment, substantially domestic; an asserted large end-market does not establish a company market share. [S01][S02][S04]

Economic value lies in engineering accuracy, welding and fabrication capability, approval, timely delivery and conversion economics, rather than owning steel price exposure. Management describes steel-price variation clauses, but fixed conversion and transport components still create margin risk. Customer-supplied-material conversion jobs can increase production while reducing gross billed steel revenue; management attributed about ₹40 crore of FY26 revenue compression to that mix. This is a management explanation, not a verified counterfactual sale. Historical interbranch transfers are eliminated in the offer-document revenue series. [S02][S07]

Cash is tied up before dispatch and certification. Work in progress of ₹100.2488 crore dominates FY26 inventory, with ₹50.2714 crore trade receivables and ₹6.7264 crore retention across current/noncurrent balances. The large project customers can be creditworthy while still imposing approval delays and strong bargaining power. FY25 top-three customers represent 96.61% of revenue, including an unnamed 53.87% customer. The analysis does not guess that customer's identity. Order announcements are not recognized revenue; customer advances, supplier credit, cash credit, letters of credit and channel financing are economically different sources of financing and must not be collapsed into a clean cash balance.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The proposed advantage is technical fabrication and approved-vendor execution. Mechanism: complex geometry, welding quality and plant-specific delivery requirements raise qualification friction. Evidence: railway/industrial project experience, management-reported RDSO capability and repeat orders. Durability: useful if technical staffing, quality systems and delivery remain dependable. Failure mode: competing approved vendors, a delayed plant, customer insourcing or procurement pressure can transfer the surplus back to customers. This supports a contestable 5/10 moat, not a structural monopoly. [S01][S02]

Interarch is a stronger balance-sheet reference: its April 2026 CRISIL rationale describes FY25 standalone revenue ₹1,454 crore, interest coverage 16.5× and negligible gearing, compared with Karbonsteel's much smaller scale and roughly 1.90× FY26 EBIT coverage. EPACK Prefab's FY26 report gives consolidated revenue ₹1,525 crore, EBITDA ₹160 crore and PAT ₹93 crore; its broader prefab/EPS perimeter and product mix are not a direct fabricated-tonne comparison. Pennar is a more leveraged diversified engineering comparator: CARE's March 2026 report gives FY25 consolidated revenue ₹3,229.99 crore, PBILDT ₹314.22 crore and coverage 2.63×. These different dates and definitions are explicit. They benchmark business and funding economics, not a same-day valuation league table. [S20][S21][S22]

There is no defensible company market-share denominator in the reviewed records. Large names in the customer list establish commercial access, not pricing power. The incumbent relationship can lower selling cost and assist repeat work while simultaneously creating concentration risk. No peer multiple is copied into the base case; 5/7/9× terminal EBITDA are disclosed analyst ranges, subject to scale, margin and financing stress.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The primary-source revenue sequence is FY22 ₹88.8316 crore, FY23 ₹155.5803 crore, FY24 ₹218.3376 crore, FY25 ₹273.0535 crore and FY26 ₹300.8775 crore. Annual additions are ₹66.7487 crore, ₹62.7573 crore, ₹54.7159 crore and ₹27.8240 crore. FY22 differs from original gross trading/revenue presentations because interbranch transfers are eliminated; it also represents a pandemic/trading-mix period. FY23–FY26 was selected before scoring as the more relevant three-year fabrication window. Its CAGR is 24.5886%, not the less comparable aggregator five-year number. Five- and ten-year comparable primary CAGRs are ND because the necessary earlier observations are not verified. [S01][S02][S03]

Latest full-year growth is 10.19%. H1FY26 revenue ₹139.7028 crore compares with ₹105.9534 crore in H1FY25, approximately 31.85% growth. H2FY26 ₹161.1747 crore compares with ₹167.1001 crore, a 3.55% decline. Do not double H 1 into TTM or mix a quarterly series with half-year reporting. H1FY27 results were not available by the cutoff; the latest comparable twelve-month result is FY26. [S10][S11]

Management reports 22.8% growth in handled tonnage to 34,900 MT, supporting real activity despite weaker billing growth. The volume figure includes labor/conversion work and cannot be divided by only nominal installed manufacturing capacity to infer a clean utilization ratio. A full annual price/volume/new-customer bridge is ND. Broad manufacturing economics and common operating perimeter support a Medium-confidence REV8, without claiming every rupee is volume-driven or awarding an extra TAM, small-base or expansion bonus.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible demand is evidenced by March 2026 executable orders ₹253 crore, May 2026 management-reported orders ₹353 crore and an August 29 announcement of ₹67.14 crore purchase orders deliverable by 3 March 2027. The ₹150 crore bid pipeline is excluded from firm backlog. The dates are not additive: without opening orders plus intake minus execution/cancellations, there is no verified October closing backlog. Margin, cancellation, advance and customer concentration terms are incompletely disclosed. [S01][S07][S09]

The annual report targets 54,000 MT capacity by October 2026 and illustrates ₹540 crore sales at ₹100/kg. This is a bottom-up capacity arithmetic check, not a forecast or commissioning certificate. The base model grows at 10%, 15%, 12%, 10%, 8%, 8% across FY27–FY32, yielding about ₹529 crore terminal LTM revenue. The bull case reaches about ₹718 crore, above the stated capacity at unchanged realization, and therefore requires further capacity/productivity investment beyond simply completing the present project. Capex ratios in the model may prove inadequate under that case; the bull is not independently verified. [S01][S07]

The same standalone organic perimeter supports an aggregate incremental bridge. FY23–FY26 NOPAT at 26% tax rises from ₹10.709724 crore to ₹21.487454 crore; book capital excluding all cash/deposits rises from ₹63.8255 crore to ₹156.5178 crore. The ₹10.77773 crore numerator over ₹92.6923 crore additional capital gives 11.6274%. Retaining all cash/deposits as committed capital reduces it to 11.0036%. Additional fixed assets/CWIP of ₹43.7056 crore reconcile ₹52.7918 crore capex less ₹9.0863 crore DA within rounding; other net capital adds ₹48.9867 crore. This residual includes working capital, tax/provision and advance effects, not pure ONWC. Current-maturity and expense-creditor regroupings do not alter aggregate equity plus debt. [S01][S02][S10]

The earlier FY23–FY25 proxy was 21.82–22.85%, while FY26 incremental returns are negative and ₹23.483 crore CWIP is still immature. CAP 5 reflects mixed windows and uncertain improvement, not a claim all expansion earns 11%. The analyst nominal INR post-tax cost-of-capital range is 12–16%, reflecting small scale, concentration, credit and SME risks; it is not an observed WACC. Legacy utilization and price/mix cannot be fully separated from new-asset returns, so this is not project IRR. Including CWIP prevents premature exclusion of committed capital. GQS is 6.30, but the reporting/funding holds remain.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters Shrenik Kirit Shah and Mittal Shrenik Shah retain control. The FY26 annual report records director remuneration ₹1.05 crore, office rent ₹0.66 crore and related-party borrowing balances around ₹3.5606 crore. These are disclosed commercial exposures, not proof of abuse. The remuneration alone is approximately 10% of FY26 PAT; rent and financing terms deserve continued scrutiny. CARO's in-year director-interested corporate-guarantee statement needs reconciliation with note 32's zero closing corporate guarantees, rather than being automatically called hidden debt. [S01]

The September 2025 IPO comprised 3,039,600 fresh shares for ₹48.32964 crore and 690,000 promoter-sale shares for ₹10.971 crore. Only fresh proceeds fund the company. Issued shares rise from 11,102,222 to 14,141,822: share-count expansion is 27.38%, while pre-issue holders' ownership dilution is 21.49%. A bonus is not economic dilution; weighted-average EPS shares and current issued claims are distinct. No new warrants/convertibles were established in the reviewed period; future borrowing or issuance authority is not proof of cash availability. [S01][S02][S13]

Promises versus delivery: November 2025 CRISIL described expansion completion by FY26 end; the June 2026 call and later annual report move completion to October 2026. The June transcript repeatedly mislabels fiscal years and says October 2025, so the dated annual report's October 2026 clarification is used, with the original error retained. FY26 volume and sales rose, but EBITDA/PAT fell and Khopoli was consolidated. Management attributes the shortfall to gas/labor disruption, customer billing mix, rental and relocation costs. Those explanations are meaningful counterevidence, but a repeated delivery/ramp issue remains. G1 is Conditional, not Fail; a clean public-issue history alone would not justify a high governance score.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The entire FY26 main statutory opinion, CARO and separate IFC report was inspected. Main and IFC opinions are unmodified. However CARO says no IPO/FPO money was raised during the year despite the documented September 2025 IPO. Explicit audit-trail reporting and the bank-stock/book-debt quarterly reconciliation table were not located in the package; absence is reported as a scope gap, not a clean conclusion. Note 37.7 also says no plant and machinery despite manufacturing assets. These look compatible with template/reporting defects, but that is an inference rather than an auditor explanation. [S01]

The annual report cash-flow statement closes at negative ₹2.7163 crore while its reconciliation gives positive ₹0.8841 crore. The earlier May 30 results use cash capex ₹29.6669 crore rather than annual-report ₹33.2673 crore, exactly bridging ₹3.6004 crore and reconciling the cash. Both originals were visually checked. Therefore no claim of missing or diverted cash is warranted. Preferred diagnostic capex uses the earlier internally coherent figure, while both reported figures remain visible and a formal correction is still outstanding. FY25 CFO also changes from original ₹4.5697 crore to RHP ₹4.6832 crore to latest comparative ₹9.1027 crore. Gratuity explains the first ₹0.1135 crore change. The later ₹4.4195 crore CFO change is fully bridged numerically: operating profit before working capital −0.1200; advances −0.0001; other current assets −0.0585; trade payables −4.8325; other current liabilities +9.4205; short provisions +0.0315; tax −0.0214 crore. The balance-sheet other-liability increase ₹21.7374 crore is approximately expense-creditor regrouping ₹15.0901 crore plus current debt maturities ₹6.6473 crore, within ₹0.0002 crore rounding. This clarifies presentation, but is not a formal explanation of every underlying opening classification. [S01][S02][S10][S18]

The H1FY26 reviewer reports hybrid stock records, unpaid income tax ₹4.0323 crore, pending ICICI charge registration and missing balance confirmations. It obtained subsequent-realization comfort on transactions and did not modify its conclusion. FY26 notes report no pending charges and CARO no undisputed dues outstanding over six months, important later counterevidence but not a complete settlement schedule. Receivables over one year remain ₹2.56 crore; inventory is dominated by WIP. [S11][S01][S10]

FY26 EBITDA ₹32.6727 crore and PAT ₹10.5078 crore are not normalized upward. Claimed PAT ₹16.56 crore does not equal reported PAT plus the listed ₹5.89 crore pretax addbacks, and their tax effect is not supplied. Bad debts also appear in FY24 restatement, weakening the assertion that collection losses are permanently nonrecurring. G2 remains Hold on the combined unresolved reporting package, not on the disproven premise that ₹3.6004 crore cash vanished.

sections.title: Valuation, Funding & Scenario Analysis
sections.text:
At ₹104.10 and 14,141,822 shares, equity value is ₹147.2164 crore. Current full-share reported earnings are ₹7.43 per share, giving 14.01× P/E versus the historical weighted-average EPS ₹8.22. Debt is ₹60.0642 crore after adding ₹4.716 crore current maturities once; netting only ₹0.8841 crore cash gives conservative net debt ₹59.1801 crore and EV ₹206.3965 crore, or 6.32× FY26 EBITDA. Deposits ₹17.8001 crore are not treated as freely distributable surplus. Operating land is not separately added. [S01][M1][Q1]

All three cases include annual revenue, margins, taxes, working capital, capex, finance costs, amortization, cash floors, shares and exact October entry/exit stubs. Finance is not silently halved after IPO: FY26 ordinary interest ₹6.9437 crore calibrates the debt-linked component; LC/bill costs ₹7.7755 crore and processing ₹0.5910 crore remain proportional to revenue. An unreduced total-finance-cost/revenue stress is also retained. The March opening is bridged to entry, so a pre-entry deficit cannot be ignored. Existing revolving debt is only assumed to roll in diagnostics; no new bank headroom is invented. Residual IPO ₹6.39 crore is drawn once by purpose, opening tax payable ₹3.8174 crore (not asserted overdue) and capital creditors ₹0.1029 crore are paid once, operating rentals stay in costs, and remaining gratuity is reserved at exit. Restricted deposits are not released into terminal equity. [S01][S04][S07]

The conservative baseline excludes unverified FD releases and uses a policy buffer of max(₹3 crore, 1% revenue). Its opening breach is an assumption, not a factual liquidity failure. A 54-case matrix varies 0/50/100% availability of the remaining ₹11.4101 crore FDs, opening versus entry release, and reserves of ₹0.5 crore flat, max(₹1 crore, 0.5% revenue), or the baseline. Those cases separately assume ₹1.43 crore IPO WC/general funds available at opening, while ₹4.91 crore capex and ₹0.05 crore debt funds are drawn only against matching uses. No deposit is counted twice. Even the base case with all unknown FDs released at opening and only ₹0.5 crore reserve first breaches at March 2028, rather than being rejected merely at opening. All tested cases breach under these operating/capex assumptions; that is not a forecast of actual failure or a claim no alternative terms could work.

Every ordinary investment output remains null because G2 and current funding are unverified. Conditional non-rescue returns also remain null after any modeled breach, including pre-entry and pre-release gaps. The separate rescue assumes equity at ₹83.28, 3% fees and explicit new shares. Base gross rescue is ₹43.02 crore, with 26.76% original-holder dilution and a 15.14% mechanical return. These are not financing terms shown to be available, and that return is not R. Negative notional cash is an unfunded deficit, never available debt.

The two-way growth/multiple grid, collections+30 days, margin−2 points, capex+25%, delayed-ramp and linked stresses are embedded. 12/15/18% hurdle sensitivity is shown only for separately labeled rescue mechanics. The reverse solver reports no feasible non-rescue funded crossing rather than a search endpoint. A 12/14/16% discount-rate by 2/4/5% terminal-growth DCF grid retains a 14% terminal ROIC and explicit reinvestment. FCFF/DCF diagnostics explicitly retain reserves, signed entry cash less required cash, reinvestment and terminal-value share; they produce no investable entry price while G2/G3 remain unresolved.

sections.title: Bear Case, Falsification & Capital Impairment
sections.text:
The most important variable is cash realization on a small number of industrial projects while capacity spending and financing payments continue. A customer defers dispatch/certification, WIP stays high, revenue and conversion margin fall, labor/rent costs persist, and bank/capital markets become less accommodating. This linked path can turn attractive nominal growth into dilution or permanent capital impairment. High concentration makes this more meaningful than a generic 20% price decline. [S01][S02][S04]

The modeled bear assumes an initial 10% revenue decline, lower 7.5–8.5% margins,39% operating working capital, delayed returns on capex and 5× exit EBITDA. It requires roughly ₹87.04 crore hypothetical gross rescue with about 42.50% original-holder dilution and a negative mechanical recapitalized return. Those numbers are stress diagnostics, not estimates of a reported default probability or a forecast of an actual equity issue. Without financing, a terminal algebraic enterprise value does not protect shareholders through an interim cash shortfall. [S01][S07]

The strongest evidence against a uniformly bearish view is the internally reconciled earlier cash-flow filing, actual FY26 receivable/inventory reductions, post-IPO debt reduction, real new orders and unmodified audit/IFC opinions. Infomerics withdrawal followed bank NOC/no-dues, so its prior non-cooperation designation must not be called a default. Conversely, CRISIL's 16 October update expressly awaits adequate information and is not a reaffirmation; old liquidity comfort should not be promoted to a current certificate. Equally it must not be erased: CRISIL's November 2025 rationale described adequate liquidity, ₹40 crore unencumbered cash in September 2025, of which ₹33 crore was earmarked for capex/debt/working capital/corporate purposes, and 91% bank-line utilization. Those are meaningful dated positive facts, not October 2026 availability. [S04][S05][S10]

Impairment risk is High as an analytical category, not Severe by default: there is no substantiated diversion, suspension or bank default. A corrected report and credible liquidity/commissioning bridge would falsify much of the hold thesis. A weaker quarter alone would not; inability to pay obligations, unexplained additional guarantees or persistent unreconciled balances would materially worsen it.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Outcome Feasibility
sections.text:
No multibagger target is assigned. Over five years,5× requires approximately 37.97% annualized share-price growth and 10× approximately 58.49%, before dividends. Company revenue growth, enterprise value, equity value and per-share return are different quantities. The relevant bridge is revenue growth times attributable margin change times original-to-final share ratio times P/E change. A recapitalization reduces the shareholder's fraction even when it increases company liquidity. [S01][S02]

At unchanged 14.01× current full-share earnings multiple and no dilution, a 5× price would require approximately ₹52.54 crore PAT; 10× about ₹105.08 crore. At 5% net margin those translate to revenue around ₹1,051 crore and ₹2,102 crore, well above the stated ₹540 crore capacity arithmetic at ₹100/kg. Higher margins or multiples reduce the revenue requirement, but introduce assumptions not independently demonstrated. Lower terminal multiples and further dilution raise the hurdle. These are feasibility arithmetic, not price targets. [S01][S07][Q1]

Management's aspiration of ₹800–1,000 crore turnover has no verified financed operating path in this record. The most useful early tests are commissioning, collections, reliable reporting and per-share earnings after the IPO. The available expansion, customer and incremental-capital evidence cannot support a 5×/10× forecast. Classification: Speculative / unsupported as an investment outcome today. It can be revisited if attributable returns and a durable funded scaling record emerge; no precise success probability is manufactured.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Financial correction: baseline annual cash gap ₹3.6004 crore, numerically bridged by earlier capex. Review the next corrected statutory filing; warning is silence or further differences, thesis-break is a material unresolvable earnings/assets issue. 2. Cashflow comparatives: reconcile FY25 CFO ₹4.5697/4.6832/9.1027 crore and debt/payable regroupings. A signed source bridge is the desired outcome, not a preferred high CFO ratio. 3. Full audit scope: obtain clear bank-stock/book-debt reconciliation and audit-trail reporting, and the corporate-guarantee rollforward. A clean main opinion alone is not the endpoint. [S01][S02][S10][S18]

4. Funding: baseline March liquid cash ₹0.8841 crore, deposits ₹17.8001 crore, debt ₹60.0642 crore and residual IPO ₹6.39 crore. Review dated available balances/headroom, lien schedules, tax settlement and remaining capex against credible stress. A real unpaid obligation or funding withdrawal is more serious than an assumed model gap. 5. Expansion:October 2026 targeted 54,000 MT; require commissioning, customer acceptance, throughput and gross-margin evidence rather than only shed construction. 6. Customer concentration/order conversion: FY25 top 3 share 96.61%; August ₹67.14 crore delivery due 3 March 2027. Track confirmed backlog rollforward, cancellations, margins and cash, not pipeline headlines. [S01][S02][S09]

7. Collections: baseline AR ₹50.2714 crore, >1 year ₹2.56 crore and retention ₹6.7264 crore. Investigate persistent aged-balance growth or additional write-offs; WIP and retention should not quietly replace reduced debtors. 8. Per-share performance: current-share EPS ₹7.43 and EBITDAmargin 10.86%; test recovery without untaxed addbacks or unexpected dilution. 9. Ratings:October 16 information request needs resolution; no automatic assumption that an unchanged rating is a fresh review. 10. Execution: complete missing July 24/August 25/October 14 turnover/no-print records, refresh 800-share lot, restrictions and live depth before implementation. These are research review triggers, not scheduled reminders or trading instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved, with research priority on financial-report reconciliation and financing/commissioning verification. The company is not classified Avoid — governance, Distressed/default or an evidence-backed compounder. BQS 5.00 and GQS 6.30 describe mixed historical business/growth quality. IAS is NS because reliable current funding, investment returns, expectations and liquidity inputs are missing; G2/G3 holds exclude investment ranking. The framework matrix cannot manufacture a point from missing evidence. [S01][S04]

For a prospective investor, even a seemingly low 6.32× EBITDA does not establish a funded return. The ₹104.73 illustrative 15% hurdle entry in the separate hypothetical base-rescue calculation is not an ordinary entry price or recommendation: it presumes recapitalization on terms not shown to be available, plus all the operating assumptions. All ordinary entries remain null. For an existing holder, the most relevant questions are whether the reporting correction is formalized, liquidity is genuinely available and the delayed expansion converts into cash per share. No holdings, acquisition price, tax position or portfolio concentration were supplied, so no buy/sell or sizing instruction is inferred. [S01][S07][Q1]

At the reference close,6 lots cost ₹499,680 and 7 lots ₹582,960. A precisely ₹5 lakh allocation is not feasible in 800-share increments. Historical whole-lot capacity and incomplete turnover data cannot promise an exit, particularly on one-sided or circuit days. Price fluctuations do not resolve structural liquidity. Evidence-backed improvements could change the hold without a new promotional story; worsening verified bank or reporting facts could change it in the other direction. The analysis is informational, not personalized investment advice.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary issuer annual report, offer documents, original accounts, half-year results, management call, order announcements and rating-agency records anchor the analysis. The main annual report is available from the issuer and an exchange-filing mirror; the decisive pages were visually inspected. An earlier results filing supplies the exact numerical counterbridge to the annual capex/cash inconsistency. Management claims are explicitly distinguished from audited historical disclosures and analyst assumptions. Sources were collected after cutoff, but only document content dated by 20 October 2026 and market rows through 19 October are used. [S01][S02][S03][S10][S11]

Three primary peer records provide different economic comparisons, not a current peer valuation screen. The official interoperability master establishes identity/lot/issued claims, while secondary OHLCV supports only a dated close and turnover proxies. Missing daily records are unknown, not zero-volume days. Direct exchange PDF access was unavailable on one route; issuer copies and the verified public filing mirror supplied originals. No source landing page is passed off as the underlying accounts. [S20][S21][S22][M1][Q1]

Open questions are the corrected full annual/audit package; prior cash-flow and debt/payable classifications; audit-trail and bank-stock reporting; corporate-guarantee scope; exact settlement of old tax/charge issues; usable FD/bank liquidity; actual expansion commissioning; project/organic incremental returns; backlog conversion and complete trading observations. The model's cash floor, tax, margin, growth, working-capital ratios, capex, debt rollovers, exit multiples, reserve treatment and rescue terms are analyst assumptions, not management promises or available facilities. Original documents, OCR, images and shareholder-level identifiers remain outside source-safe analytical backups. Those backups reproduce calculations from safe extracts and retain public source URLs/hashes; they do not contain originals or independently reauthenticate the primary filings.
